title: Annotatio II §.IX: Marburg determination does not free Luther from corporal-in-bread / subtilior consub
pass_a_gloss: Although we follow none who would free Luther’s Determination of the Marburg Colloquy — conceived in these words: (Although however whether the true body and Blood of Christ be corporally present in the bread and wine of the Lord’s Supper, we have not agreed at this time &c.) — from a corporal presence of Christ’s Body in or with the bread, and so from the subtler Consubstantiation; since those words most expressly confess not only the presence of Christ’s true Body in the Supper, but also a corporal mode of presence, nay this corporal mode of presence in the bread itself. And therefore we cannot but hint, in the place of a colophon, in three words as they say, by what Difficulties we observe pressed the Corporal presence of Christ’s body in the bread to be vindicated for either the Crasser alone or also the Subtler Consubstantiation, at least Luther’s.
pass_b_english: Marburg’s determination (we have not agreed whether the true body and blood are corporally present in the bread and wine) does not free Luther from corporal presence in or with the bread — nor from subtler Consubstantiation.
Those words confess not presence alone but a corporal mode in the bread itself.
Colophon: watch the difficulties that press corporal-in-bread presence for crassior or subtilior (at least Luther’s) Consubstantiation.
source_text: Utut nulli assequamur, quomodo Lutheri Determinatio Colloquii Marpurgensis, his scil. concepta verbis: (Etsi autem, an verum corpus & Sanguis Christi corporaliter in pane & vino Coenæ Domini præsens sit, hoc tempore non concordavimus &c.) à Corporis Christi præsentia in vel cum pane, corporali, adeoque à subtiliori Consubstantiatione, expediri possit; cum verba ista non præsentiam duntaxat veri Corporis Christi in Coena, sed & modum præsentiæ corporalem, quin corporalem hunc præsentiæ modum, in ipso pane, disertissimè profiteantur. Eoque non possumus non colophonis locô, tribus quod aiunt verbis, innuere, quibus Difficultatibus Corporalem corporis Christi in pane præsentiam, sive soli Crassiori, sive & Subtiliori, saltem Lutheri, Consubstantiationi vindicandam, pressam advertamus.
